:::{#thm-closest-point}
#### The orthogonal projection is the closest point

Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a subspace of $\reals^p$, let $\vecf{y} \in \reals^p$,
and let $\vecf{u}$ be the orthogonal projection of $\vecf{y}$ onto $\mathcal{S}$
(@def-orthogonal-projection).
Then for every $\vecf{w} \in \mathcal{S}$,

$$
\norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{u}} \le \norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{w}},
$$

with equality only when $\vecf{w} = \vecf{u}$.

:::

::: proof

By @def-orthogonal-projection, $\vecf{y} - \vecf{u} \in \mathcal{S}^\perp$.
Both $\vecf{u}$ and $\vecf{w}$ are in $\mathcal{S}$,
so $\vecf{u} - \vecf{w} = \vecf{u} + (-1)\,\vecf{w} \in \mathcal{S}$ (@def-subspace),
and therefore $(\vecf{y} - \vecf{u}) \perp (\vecf{u} - \vecf{w})$
(@def-orthogonal-complement). Then

$$
\ba
\norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{w}}^2
&= \norm{(\vecf{y} - \vecf{u}) + (\vecf{u} - \vecf{w})}^2
&& \text{(add and subtract } \vecf{u} \text{)}
\\
&= \norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{u}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{u} - \vecf{w}}^2
&& \text{(Pythagorean theorem, @thm-norm-sum-square)}
\\
&\ge \norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{u}}^2,
&& \text{(} \norm{\vecf{u} - \vecf{w}}^2 \ge 0 \text{, @thm-norm-properties)}
\ea
$$

with equality exactly when $\norm{\vecf{u} - \vecf{w}} = 0$,
that is, when $\vecf{w} = \vecf{u}$ (@thm-norm-properties, part 1).
Taking nonnegative square roots preserves the inequality.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-closest-point}
#### No point of the line is closer

In @exm-orthogonal-projection,
$\vecf{y} = (3, 1, 2)$ has projection $\vecf{u} = (2, 2, 0)$
onto $\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1, 0)}$,
at distance $\norm{(1, -1, 2)} = \sqrt{6}$.
Another point of $\mathcal{S}$, such as $\vecf{w} = (3, 3, 0)$,
is farther:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\norm{\vecf{y} - \vecf{w}} &= \norm{(0, -2, 2)} \\
&= \sqrt{8} \\
&> \sqrt{6},
\end{aligned}
$$

and the difference of squares is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\norm{\vecf{u} - \vecf{w}}^2 &= \norm{(-1, -1, 0)}^2 \\
&= 2 \\
&= 8 - 6,
\end{aligned}
$$

by the Pythagorean theorem (@thm-norm-sum-square),
since $\vecf{y} - \vecf{u} \in \mathcal{S}^\perp$ and $\vecf{u} - \vecf{w} \in \mathcal{S}$.

:::
